senses.definition_en: Catalan secessionist

examples.english: “Catalufo” is a derogatory term applied not to Catalans, but to nationalists, similar to “charnego,” which catalufos use to refer to people originally from other regions. There is one difference: the term charnego belittles someone simply because they were born somewhere else, whereas catalufo disparages those who think and act in ways that are deeply offensive to the rest of Spaniards.
examples.ref: 2007 September 27, “Catalanes y Catalufos”, in Libertad Digital, Madrid:
examples.text: “Catalufo” es un término despectivo aplicado no a los catalanes, sino a los nacionalistas, similar al de “charnego” con que los catalufos designan al oriundo de otras regiones. Con una diferencia: la voz charnego rebaja a alguien por el mero hecho de haber nacido en otro lugar, mientras que catalufo desprecia a quienes piensan y actúan de modo muy ofensivo para el resto de los españoles.
examples.translation: “Catalufo” is a derogatory term applied not to Catalans, but to nationalists, similar to “charnego,” which catalufos use to refer to people originally from other regions. There is one difference: the term charnego belittles someone simply because they were born somewhere else, whereas catalufo disparages those who think and act in ways that are deeply offensive to the rest of Spaniards.

glosses: Catalan secessionist

examples.english: At that moment, another street vendor approached from behind and snatched some of the merchandise from the officers, after which he ran off with a pronounced smile on his face.
examples.ref: 2015 November 8, “Con la mercancía a cuestas”, in El País:
examples.text: En ese instante, otro mantero se acercó por la espalda y arrebató a los agentes parte de la mercancía, tras lo cual salió a la carrera con una pronunciada sonrisa en la cara.
examples.translation: At that moment, another street vendor approached from behind and snatched some of the merchandise from the officers, after which he ran off with a pronounced smile on his face.

examples.english: The death of a Senegalese street vendor this Thursday in the Madrid neighborhood of Lavapiés sparked a wave of street protests and a massive deployment of police, who charged and shot rubber bullets to disperse protestors who set fire to dumpsters and parked cars in the area.

examples.text: La muerte de un mantero senegalés este jueves en el barrio madrileño de Lavapiés desató una oleada de protestas callejeras y un amplio despliegue policial con cargas y pelotas de goma para dispersar a manifestantes que incendiaron contenedores y vehículos estacionados en la zona.
examples.translation: The death of a Senegalese street vendor this Thursday in the Madrid neighborhood of Lavapiés sparked a wave of street protests and a massive deployment of police, who charged and shot rubber bullets to disperse protestors who set fire to dumpsters and parked cars in the area.
